name: 25784-blazedit-8b-1gpu
model: NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct -- the ungated mirror of the gated `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct`. Same weights; a mirror, not a substitution.
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1. One engine, one card.
architecture: LlamaForCausalLM, dense, 32 layers, 32 query heads, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, hidden 4096, vocab 128256, bf16, 8.03B params = 16.1 GB of weights.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=1, bounded at 96 requests / 1800 s safety, warmup the first 10% by completion.
workload: guidellm `json_file`, single turn, no prefix_buckets: `configs/data/blazedit-5kchar-96.jsonl`, all 96 rows of `vdaita/edit_5k_char` (Blazedit, https://github.com/ise-uiuc/blazedit), rebuilt offline. Each request is a ~5.9k-character Python source file plus a natural-language change request and the expected answer is the whole rewritten file; ~1.4k prompt tokens (max 2042 on the wire, after the chat template), output capped at 4000 tokens, EOS honoured, greedy.
purpose: A code-editing assistant rewriting whole Python files from change requests, one request at a time on a single GPU.
launch:
# The engine is the commit named by configs/setupcard.md `commit_id:`; the interpreter that
# holds it is configs/env.yaml `venv:`. Engine args are that commit's, not a later vLLM's.
model: NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
speculative-config: {"method": "ngram", "num_speculative_tokens": 12, "prompt_lookup_min": 3, "prompt_lookup_max": 5}
max-model-len: 8192
tensor-parallel-size: 1
dtype: bfloat16
max-num-seqs: 8
enable-prefix-caching: false
